proposals.before: In the second year of Yuanshi, Marquis of Xindu Wang Mang raised the fallen and continued the cut off; he informed the Grand Empress Dowager and established Nian’s younger brother’s son Ruyi as King of Guangzong, to serve the Filial Queen of Dai.
proposals.after: In the second year of Yuanshi, Marquis of Xindu Wang Mang raised the fallen and continued the cut off; he informed the Grand Empress Dowager and established Nian’s younger brother’s son Ruyi as King of Guangzong, to continue the ancestral sacrifices of King Xiao of Dai.
proposals.reason: 奉代孝王后 means continuing King Xiao of Dai’s ancestral line/posterity, not serving a “Filial Queen.”

proposals.before: Two years later Wang Mang reported to the Grand Empress Dowager and established Yin, a registrar of Pei Commandery and a descendant several generations removed from King Xiao, as king of Liang to continue the line of King Xiao.
proposals.after: Two years later Wang Mang reported to the Grand Empress Dowager and established Yin, a registrar of Pei Commandery and a great-great-great-grandson’s great-grandson of King Xiao, as king of Liang to continue King Xiao’s ancestral line.
proposals.reason: Keep 玄孫之曾孫 specificity; 奉孝王后 is sacrificial succession of the line, already partly right in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Wu and Chu were broken, and as for those whom Liang killed and captured, it was roughly half with Han.
proposals.after: Wu and Chu were broken, and those whom Liang killed and captured were roughly half with the Han forces.
proposals.reason: 漢中分 is ‘shared half-and-half with Han,’ not the place-name Hanzhong.

decisions.reason: 奉代孝王后 means to continue the sacrificial posterity of 代孝王 (King Xiao of Dai); the before misreads 后 as “queen” and invents a “Filial Queen of Dai,” while the proposed after restores the correct sense.

The before already correctly renders 奉孝王后 as continuing King Xiao’s line, and “descendant several generations removed” adequately glosses 玄孫之曾孫; the proposed “great-great-great-grandson’s great-grandson” is awkward and overcounts 玄孫, so the change is not an accurate repair.
The before already takes 與漢中分 as sharing roughly half with Han, not as the place-name 漢中; adding “the Han forces” is only stylistic smoothing of accurate English.
